subject: pharmacology
title: Antacids, Eradication Regimens, and Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers

steps.tx: A synthetic methyl ester analogue of prostaglandin E1 specifically indicated for the prevention of NSAID-induced peptic ulcers is **misoprostol**. By activating EP3 receptors on parietal cells, misoprostol couples to inhibitory Gi proteins to suppress adenylyl cyclase, decreasing intracellular cyclic AMP and basal acid secretion. Concurrently, it stimulates epithelial EP2 and EP4 receptors, enhancing mucus and bicarbonate secretion and increasing mucosal blood flow. Its clinical utility is limited by dose-dependent diarrhea and abdominal cramps, and it is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to abortifacient actions.
steps.say: Misoprostol couples to Gi proteins to suppress acid while enhancing mucosal blood flow and cytoprotection.

nodes.label: Activation of parietal EP3 receptors via inhibitory Gi protein
Suppression of adenylyl cyclase and decreased intracellular cyclic AMP
Stimulation of epithelial EP2/EP4 receptors: enhanced mucus and bicarbonate secretion

steps.tx: Weak basic chemical compounds administered to directly neutralize secreted hydrochloric acid within the gastric lumen are **antacids**. Formulated as combinations of magnesium hydroxide (fast-acting, osmotic laxative) and aluminum hydroxide (slow-acting, constipating, astringent), these agents neutralize gastric acid to elevate intragastric pH above 3.5 without altering acid production. This inhibits pepsin proteolytic activity and relieves heartburn symptoms rapidly within minutes. In contrast, systemic absorbable antacids like sodium bicarbonate provoke systemic metabolic alkalosis and fluid retention in heart failure.
steps.say: Antacids neutralize luminal hydrochloric acid directly, combining magnesium and aluminum salts to balance bowel habits.

left.title: Magnesium Hydroxide (Milk of Magnesia)
points: Rapid onset of chemical acid neutralization
Reacts with gastric acid to form unabsorbed magnesium chloride
Exerts osmotic laxative effect, predisposing to watery diarrhea
Contraindicated in severe chronic kidney disease (hypermagnesemia)

right.title: Aluminum Hydroxide Gel
points: Slow, sustained chemical neutralization of luminal acid
Forms unabsorbed aluminum chloride complexes, provoking constipation
Binds dietary phosphate in gut, lowering serum phosphate
Risk of microcytic anemia and aluminum neurotoxicity in uremia

steps.tx: The classic fourteen-day first-line antimicrobial eradication regimen for gastric and duodenal ulcers colonized by H. pylori is **Helicobacter pylori triple therapy**. Comprising a standard-dose proton pump inhibitor, clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily, and amoxicillin 1000 mg twice daily (or metronidazole in penicillin allergy), this combination achieves bacterial eradication by suppressing acid to optimize antibiotic stability while inhibiting bacterial protein and cell wall synthesis. However, rising global clarithromycin resistance exceeding fifteen percent has shifted first-line recommendations toward bismuth-based quadruple therapy.
steps.say: Helicobacter pylori triple therapy combines a proton pump inhibitor, clarithromycin, and amoxicillin for fourteen days.

rows: PPI twice daily + Clarithromycin 500 mg + Amoxicillin 1 g
Only recommended where local clarithromycin resistance <15%
Preferred first-line regimen in high clarithromycin resistance areas
PPI + Amoxicillin 1 g + Clarithromycin 500 mg + Metronidazole
High eradication rates without requiring heavy metal bismuth salts

steps.tx: A rare hypergastrinemic disorder caused by a neuroendocrine gastrin-secreting tumor located in the duodenum or pancreas is **Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**. Continuous autonomous release of gastrin hyper-stimulates parietal and enterochromaffin-like cells, causing massive gastric acid hypersecretion with basal acid output exceeding 15 mEq/hr, prominent mucosal rugal hypertrophy, multiple atypical peptic ulcers refractory to standard therapy, and secretory diarrhea with steatorrhea caused by acid inactivation of pancreatic lipase. Medical management requires exceptionally high doses of proton pump inhibitors, often doubling or tripling standard regimens.
steps.say: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome causes massive acid hypersecretion from an autonomous gastrinoma, requiring high-dose PPIs.

nodes.label: Unregulated gastrin hypersecretion into systemic circulation
Marked trophic hyperplasia of gastric parietal and ECL cells
Basal acid output >15 mEq/hr: severe refractory peptic ulcers and steatorrhea

steps.tx: A chronic condition where retrograde transit of acidic gastric contents into the esophagus provokes troublesome symptoms or mucosal breaks, known as **GERD** (gastroesophageal reflux disease). Pathologically driven by transient lower esophageal sphincter relaxations, low resting sphincter pressure, and delayed esophageal acid clearance, reflux of hydrochloric acid and pepsin produces retrosternal pyrosis and acid regurgitation. Long-term acid exposure induces erosive reflux esophagitis, peptic strictures, and premalignant intestinal metaplasia of squamous epithelium known as Barrett esophagus, responding best to step-down proton pump inhibitor regimens.
steps.say: GERD causes retrosternal pyrosis from transient sphincter relaxations, predisposing to erosive esophagitis and Barrett esophagus.

vis.alt: Pathophysiology of acid secretion and peptic mucosal injury
vis.caption: Gastroduodenal and lower esophageal mucosal defenses illustrating acid aggression and mucosal barrier breakdown in reflux and ulcer disease.

steps.tx: The physiological resurgence of excessive gastric acid production occurring following the abrupt discontinuation of prolonged proton pump inhibitor therapy is **rebound acid hypersecretion**. During chronic PPI therapy, persistent elevation of intragastric pH removes negative feedback inhibition on antral G-cells, resulting in secondary hypergastrinemia. Circulating gastrin exerts a potent trophic effect, causing marked hyperplasia of histamine-secreting ECL cells and parietal cells. Upon sudden drug withdrawal, these hypertrophied cells generate a surge of acid exceeding baseline levels, causing severe recurrent dyspepsia that mandates gradual dose tapering.
steps.say: Abrupt PPI cessation triggers rebound acid hypersecretion because secondary hypergastrinemia induces parietal cell hyperplasia.

nodes.label: Chronic daily proton pump inhibitor therapy (months to years)
Achlorhydria removes negative feedback: secondary hypergastrinemia
Trophic hyperplasia of histamine-secreting ECL and parietal cells
Abrupt drug cessation unmasks hyperplastic cells: severe acid hypersecretion

steps.tx: A modern potassium-competitive acid blocker that represents a breakthrough in acid-peptic pharmacology is **vonoprazan**. Unlike traditional proton pump inhibitors, vonoprazan does not require an acidic environment for bioactivation and does not form covalent disulfide bonds. Instead, it acts as a lipophilic weak base that directly, reversibly, and competitively inhibits the potassium-binding site of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme. Exhibiting a pKa of 9.3, vonoprazan provides an ultra-fast onset of action, achieves near-complete acid suppression from the very first dose, and maintains gastric pH above 4 for twenty-four hours.
steps.say: Vonoprazan competitively blocks the potassium-binding site on proton pumps, delivering rapid, 24-hour acid suppression.

left.title: Vonoprazan (Potassium-Competitive / P-CAB)
points: Direct competitive inhibition of K+ binding site on proton pump
Acid-independent activation; full efficacy from the first oral dose
Maintains intragastric pH >4 for 24 hours (superior nocturnal control)
Superior eradication rates in clarithromycin-resistant H. pylori

right.title: Omeprazole (Proton Pump Inhibitor)
points: Prodrug requiring acid canaliculus protonation for activation
Covalent irreversible disulfide bonding with Cys813 residue
Requires 3 to 5 days of repeated dosing to reach steady-state block
Maintains intragastric pH >4 for approximately 14 hours daily

steps.tx: The premalignant histological transformation of the distal esophageal squamous epithelium into specialized columnar epithelium with intestinal goblet cells is **Barrett esophagus**. Arising as a defensive adaptation to chronic, repetitive acid and bile reflux in long-standing GERD, this specialized intestinal metaplasia confers a thirty-to-forty-fold increased risk of developing esophageal adenocarcinoma. Clinical management combines lifelong aggressive acid suppression with high-dose proton pump inhibitors to prevent neoplastic progression alongside periodic surveillance upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with four-quadrant biopsies taken every two centimeters.
steps.say: Barrett esophagus is specialized columnar metaplasia from chronic acid reflux that increases esophageal adenocarcinoma risks.

rows: Immediate repeat confirmation by expert pathologist
Endoscopic mucosal resection and radiofrequency ablation
Staging with endoscopic ultrasound and CT
